text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.

-Pressure on the Central Bank to cut interest rates is increasing after Leif Eide, head of market operations at the bank, told Aftenposten on Tuesday that there was no reason why Norwegian money-market rates should be higher than in Germany.

-The Justice Ministry will extend police rights to expel foreigners without residency permits. At the moment police authorities must seek approval from the Immigration Office before forcing foreigners to leave Norway.

-European shipyards have had a difficult year but Kvaerner ASA posted large profits in its shipbuilding division. According to a report from Norwegian shipbroker Bassoe, Japan and Korea strengthened their position in the market in 1996.

-Norsk Hydro President and Chief Executive Officer Egil Myklebust says state ownership in Norwegian industry is too high. The Norwegian state holds 51 percent of shares in industrial giant Norsk Hydro.

-Stein Erik Hagen, head of one of Norway's largest grocery firms the Hakon Group, has begun an initiative to increase cooperation between breweries in order to weaken the domination of food conglomerate Orkla ASA in the Norwegian beer market .
